attempts.plan:
1. Read the two series (first-half and second-half 2012 recorded-crime rates) and the neighbor list into pandas structures keyed by borough name.  

2. Handle missing values:  
   • Find boroughs whose first-half OR second-half value is NaN (1 borough is missing in each column, possibly the same borough).  
   • Drop those borough(s) completely from the analysis, because the change cannot be computed.  
   • Remove every reference to the dropped borough(s) from all neighbor lists so the spatial weight matrix only involves boroughs with complete data.

3. For every remaining borough, compute CHANGE = (second-half rate) − (first-half rate).

4. Build a symmetric binary spatial-weights matrix W (size n×n for the retained n boroughs): w_ij = 1 if borough i lists borough j as a neighbor (or vice-versa), otherwise 0; w_ii = 0.  
   • Row-standardize W so each row sums to 1.  
   • Compute S0 = Σ_i Σ_j w_ij, needed for Moran’s I.

5. Center the change values: z_i = CHANGE_i − mean(CHANGE).

6. Calculate Global Moran’s I:  
      I = (n / S0) · [ Σ_i Σ_j w_ij z_i z_j ]  /  Σ_i z_i²

7. Assess statistical significance with a permutation test:  
   • Randomly shuffle the z_i values across boroughs 999 times (≥500 as required).  
   • Re-compute Moran’s I for each shuffle to form the reference distribution.  
   • Two-sided p-value = proportion of permuted I’s whose absolute value ≥ |observed I|.  
   (If you prefer a one-tailed test, compare directionally; either approach must be stated with the result.)

8. Interpretation:  
   • If p < 0.05, conclude the CHANGE is spatially clustered (neighboring boroughs tend to share the same direction/magnitude of change).  
   • Otherwise, conclude the change shows no spatial clustering.

9. Report the observed Moran’s I and its p-value in the required format.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the borough-level crime data and adjacency list
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
CRIME_PATH = "chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_first_half_2012_to_second_half_2012.csv"
ADJ_PATH   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime = pd.read_csv(CRIME_PATH)
adj   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute change, drop boroughs with any missing values
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
crime["change"] = crime["second_half_2012_value"] - crime["first_half_2012_value"]
crime_clean = crime.dropna(subset=["change"]).copy()

kept_boroughs = crime_clean["borough"].tolist()
n = len(kept_boroughs)                # data points actually used

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build the binary spatial-weights matrix W (undirected)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
adj_filt = adj[
    adj["borough"].isin(kept_boroughs) & 
    adj["neighbor"].isin(kept_boroughs)
]

indexer = {b:i for i, b in enumerate(kept_boroughs)}
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)

for _, row in adj_filt.iterrows():
    i = indexer[row["borough"]]
    j = indexer[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i, j] = 1
    W[j, i] = 1          # ensure symmetry

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Global Moran’s I for the CHANGE variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
z = crime_clean["change"].values
z = z - z.mean()          # center

S0 = W.sum()
num = z @ W @ z
den = (z ** 2).sum()
I_obs = (n / S0) * (num / den)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Permutation test (999 random shuffles)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
permutations = 999
I_perm = np.empty(permutations)

rng = np.random.default_rng()
for k in range(permutations):
    z_perm = rng.permutation(z)
    I_perm[k] = (n / S0) * (z_perm @ W @ z_perm / den)

# two-sided p-value
p_val = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (permutations + 1)  # add 1 for observed

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Verdict
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
verdict = "CLUSTERED" if p_val < 0.05 else "NOT CLUSTERED"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Required prints
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (Moran's I = {I_obs}, p = {p_val})")
